# M4 · Walk-forward verdict: results

**Run:** 23 Oct 2026 on the snapshot (data through 22 Oct 2026). Every number comes from `m4_tables.md`, regenerated by `python "PS Research/m4_verdict/summarise_m4.py"`. The method is in `tola/backtest.py` (trading before tender) and `tola/delivery.py` (holding through settlement); costs are in `tola/costs.py` and `data/specs/costs.yaml`. The forward test is pre-registered in `FORWARD_TEST_PREREGISTRATION.md`.

## Verdict

**1. Only coin makers can collect the whole premium.**
- **What holding through settlement leaves:** ₹42/g on 8 g coins and ₹153/g on 1 g, before buying the coins to deliver.
- **What that implies:** delivery pays only if coins cost less than **0.27% (8 g) or 1.13% (1 g) over spot**. In the best single cycle the threshold was 2.1% and 3.75%.
- **What coins actually cost:** the cheapest we found was **3.6% (8 g) and 5.5% (1 g)** over spot, ex-GST (Augmont). Five other 1 g products cost **9.9–13.6%**.
- **Result:** delivery would have lost money in **all 18 cycles** for both pairs. The premium is the market price of small gold, set near what it costs to make. A trader can't arbitrage it away.

**2. A trader can earn a small edge from the premium's swings, not its level.**
- **The level:** shorting the premium and holding to tender has no edge (CIs span zero), because the premium doesn't fade (M3).
- **The swings:** a mean-reversion rule earns about **+5 to +15 bp a trade, net of costs**, in the current contract era (Apr 2025 on), leaving aside Jan–Mar 2026.
- **It isn't a lucky setting:** all 26 settings that traded are positive, across three pairs.
- **It isn't permanent:** the same rule lost money on GOLDPETAL/GOLDGUINEA before the Apr 2025 contract.

**3. Jan–Mar 2026 was a one-off windfall.** When the premium spiked to 160–200 bp and collapsed, the same rule made about +100 bp a trade. That quarter produced about 90% of all out-of-sample profit. A pre-registered forward test now runs to the 20 Nov finale.

**Every serious team that tested this window found the same thing:**
- **gold-rv:** its trades that closed in Jan–Mar 2026 made more than its whole test-year profit.
- **AuRA:** 78% of its development profit came from one 30 Jan 2026 exit; its untouched Apr–Oct 2026 holdout lost 1.4 bp a trade. Our rule barely traded in that window.
- **What only we add:** none of them asks who *can* collect the premium (finding 1).

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Pairs | GOLDGUINEA/GOLDTEN and GOLDPETAL/GOLDTEN (18 expired cycles, Apr 2025 – Sep 2026, plus live); GOLDPETAL/GOLDGUINEA from 2020 |
| Position | 200 g per leg, gram-matched (25 GOLDGUINEA or 200 GOLDPETAL lots against 20 GOLDTEN lots) |
| Timing | Decide on day t's close premium; fill at the next eligible day's VWAP (both legs ₹1 Cr+, neither in tender); close by the last day before tender |
| Costs | CTT, stamp duty, MCX and SEBI fees, GST, Zerodha-rate brokerage, plus **1 tick of slippage per order** (₹1 per quote unit: about 0.07 bp on GOLDTEN, 0.6 bp on GOLDPETAL). Round trip about 4–6 bp. |
| Rules | **DRIFT:** short the premium 60+ trading days out, hold to tender (no tuning). **MR(W, k):** z-score of the premium against the previous W eligible days in the cycle; enter at \|z\| > k, exit when z crosses 0. 9 configs; **10 trials per pair**. |
| Walk-forward | Each month uses the MR config with the best mean net over trades already **closed** before that month (5+ trades; otherwise W=40, k=1.5). Only those out-of-sample trades are scored. |
| Validation | Cycle-bootstrap 95% CI; random-entry null (2,000 replicas, same cycles, holds and directions); Deflated Sharpe over all 10 trials; Jan–Mar 2026 removed; break-even slippage; truncation (look-ahead) test |

**Why slippage is an assumption, not a measurement.** EDGE (Ardia, Guidotti & Kroencke 2024) on daily data gave 10–93 bp for every contract alike. It tracked daily volatility (correlation 0.89 across contracts), the same failure gold-rv hit with Roll and Corwin–Schultz. So costs use an explicit tick assumption, and every result also reports its break-even slippage.

## Evidence

### 1. Holding through settlement

Per gram, mean of 18 expired cycles, entered on the last day before tender:

| | GOLDGUINEA / GOLDTEN | GOLDPETAL / GOLDTEN |
|---|---|---|
| Futures: premium collected at settlement | +₹95 | +₹133 |
| Making charge received (short small) | +₹25 | +₹100 |
| Making charge paid (long GOLDTEN) | −₹30 | −₹30 |
| Bar resale discount (0.25%, assumed) | about −₹33 | about −₹33 |
| Vault, assay, transport (₹10/g, assumed) | −₹10 | −₹10 |
| Tender and delivery margin funding | about −₹3 | about −₹3 |
| Entry costs | about −₹3 | about −₹4 |
| **Headroom before buying coins** | **₹42** | **₹153** |
| **Break-even coin premium over spot** | **0.27%** (−0.4 to 2.1%) | **1.13%** (0.2 to 3.75%) |
| Cheapest observed coin, ex-GST | 3.6% (Augmont 8 g, 13 Oct 2026) | 5.5% (Augmont 1 g, 13 Oct 2026) |
| Other observed 1 g products, ex-GST | — | 9.9–13.6% (Joyalukkas, Malabar, MMTC-PAMP, Bangalore Refinery; 10 Jun 2026) |
| Cycles profitable at the cheapest coin price | **0 / 18** | **0 / 18** |

Coin prices are compared with that day's own polled spot. Every observation and its source is listed in `data/specs/costs.yaml`.

The verdict survives the assumptions:
- **Without the two assumed costs** (bar discount and logistics), break-even rises only to 0.60% and 1.46% (table 7).
- **Entering early** (60+ days out) raises it to 0.47% and 1.28%.
- **The best cycle** (GOLDPETAL, Jan 2026, 3.75%) owed nearly half its futures gain to the crash-day settlement gap (M3 finding 3).

**This sharpens the field's story.** arb-bound *assumes* a fabrication cost of ₹20–60 per bar. If that were true, our measured ₹153/g of headroom on 1 g coins would leave the arbitrage open every cycle. Retail prices say making and selling 1 g gold costs far more than that.

### 2. Trading before tender

**Scored trades** (DRIFT has no tuning; MR is out-of-sample only):

| Pair | Strategy | Trades | Net / trade | 95% CI | Deflated Sharpe | Random-entry p | Break-even slippage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GOLDGUINEA / GOLDTEN | DRIFT | 23 | +13.8 bp | [−32, 61] | 0.09 | n/a | 71 ticks |
| GOLDGUINEA / GOLDTEN | MR walk-forward | 29 (11 cycles) | +44.0 bp | [20, 78] | 0.88 | < 0.001 | 150 ticks |
| GOLDPETAL / GOLDTEN | DRIFT | 24 | +4.8 bp | [−39, 46] | 0.17 | n/a | 9 ticks |
| GOLDPETAL / GOLDTEN | MR walk-forward | 40 (15 cycles) | +33.5 bp | [11, 58] | 0.95 | < 0.001 | 25 ticks |
| GOLDPETAL / GOLDGUINEA | MR walk-forward | 138 (73 cycles) | −1.7 bp | [−11, 7] | 0.00 | < 0.001 | 2 ticks |

**Where the MR profit comes from:**

| MR walk-forward, out of sample | 2025 | Jan–Mar 2026 | Apr–Oct 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GOLDGUINEA / GOLDTEN | +10.5 bp (20 trades) | +118.5 bp (9) | no trades |
| GOLDPETAL / GOLDTEN | +6.2 bp (25 trades) | +95.6 bp (12) | +11.7 bp (3) |

Without Jan–Mar 2026: GOLDGUINEA **+10.5 bp [4.4, 15.3]** (20 trades) and GOLDPETAL **+6.8 bp [0.5, 15.3]** (28 trades).

**It isn't one lucky setting.** Every config, current era (contracts from Apr 2025), Jan–Mar 2026 removed, mean net bp a trade:

| | W=20 | W=40 | W=60 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GOLDGUINEA / GOLDTEN (k = 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0) | 9.5 / 11.5 / 14.2 | 7.8 / 8.7 / 13.7 | 9.8 / 11.4 / — |
| GOLDPETAL / GOLDTEN | 6.3 / 5.7 / 7.7 | 1.8 / 5.8 / 4.3 | 2.9 / 10.9 / 17.7 |
| GOLDPETAL / GOLDGUINEA | 1.8 / 1.9 / 2.9 | 4.7 / 6.5 / 5.1 | 0.9 / 7.4 / 7.9 |

All **26 of 26** settings that traded are positive. DRIFT is the only negative entry (−0.6 and −12.7 bp).

**It depends on the contract era.** GOLDPETAL/GOLDGUINEA walk-forward makes **+14.2 bp** a trade on contracts from Apr 2025 (36 trades) but **−7.3 bp** before (102 trades). The pre-2025 GOLDPETAL contract was a different market (M1–M3).

**Checks:**
- **No look-ahead:** cutting the data at 15 Feb 2026 leaves all 1,110 earlier trades identical. This is a test.
- **A spread trade, not a gold bet:** the spread leg is 100–105% of MR gross P&L.
- **Slippage doesn't decide it:** at 10 ticks per order, MR walk-forward still makes +41 and +18 bp.

## What this means for the product

- **The chooser (M5) is the core.** Since nobody but a coin maker collects the premium, the useful answer for a trader is which contract to hold and when to exit. A trader who exits before tender pays the premium's *change*; one who takes delivery pays the whole premium plus the making charge.
- **The alert log flags swings, not levels.** That's where the small edge lives. It stays quiet by default, because the rule trades rarely in calm regimes.
- **Pitch line:** "The small-lot premium is real every cycle, but it is the price of small gold. Collecting it means making 1 g coins for under about 1% over spot. Trading it pays only in its swings, and mostly in a crisis."

## Limits

- **Fills** are the next day's VWAP, which a working order can approach but isn't guaranteed. Slippage is assumed (1 tick base), with break-evens shown.
- **Sample:** 18 same-reference cycles. The current-era edge rests on 20–40 out-of-sample trades per pair. The forward test adds only a few weeks.
- **Coin prices** are two dated snapshots (13 Oct and 10 Jun 2026), retail only. Refiners' fabrication cost isn't public, hence the break-even framing.
- **The delivery leg** assumes a GST-registered participant (3% GST nets out), a 0.25% bar resale discount and ₹10/g logistics.
- **Statutory charges** come from Zerodha's published schedule, not yet checked against a contract note.
